Design choices:
- The report sits over the live monitor (z-20) rather than in the lab's modal slot, which covers the whole lab. This keeps the reference monitor (runs, QCA) and the guided drawer usable while reporting.
- The old guided two-step finish (Keep going / Confirm finish) and the one-click finish in other modes are replaced by "Finish study", then the report, then submit. This applies in every mode, including exams and the full case's diagnostic stage. The store's finishCase is unchanged for other callers.
- Territory truth uses the engine's FlowRegions: the artery is the region's own vessel or the nearest named artery on its path; the injection is the region's side. A wall beyond a CTO also accepts the collateral donor from its own injection, and a graft counts if it is not occluded and lands on the supplying artery.
- The deferral rules judge only what the lab knows: anatomy (unprotected LM, CTO, multivessel disease), diagnostic-only consent, and a complication (dissection, VF, air). Dose, place, symptoms, people, preparation and choice are offered to the learner but not graded.
- report.ts reimplements lesionIdOf as targetLesionId so the mentor does not load the engine. A test checks the two agree.
- report.ts imports debrief.ts types only, so the check registry has no runtime import cycle; registries.test.ts passes.
- The reachability report printed the same counts as before; no raises export was added to a globbed file.

The design is largely implemented:
- The finish step, StudyReport form and store fields (finishing, studyReport, beginFinish, cancelFinish, submitStudyReport) are in place. finishCase is unchanged for other callers.
- Truth is built only on submit. The registered debrief check and the Study report debrief tab are present.
- The phase becomes finish when the report opens. territory-unsupplied, anomalous-origin and cto are raised and cleared correctly, and the anomalous circumflex tips appear in the tests.
- Clinical text is sourced from the module text: Brilakis 7.3 deferral list, MINOCA wording and "ideally within 2 weeks", spasm, complete filling, graft stump. App conventions are labelled MODEL PARAMETER. Recording those in docs/realism/facts is out of scope.
- The UI uses Clinical Graphite classes and British English. Truth is not shown on live screens, and tips appear only in the guided drawer or after asking for help. Render paths do not allocate per frame.

Probes I ran (scratch vitest in the scratchpad, no repo edits) confirmed two defects:
1. An isolated left main lesion counts as multivessel disease, so ad hoc PCI on a protected left main is still flagged as a safety gap.
2. The tree's real septal branch names S1 to S12 are mapped to the anterior wall instead of the septum.

Not met (acknowledged by the builder): the plan's named scenarios and their practice links do not exist, and the browser check was not done.

findings.problem: lesionArteries(LM) returns [LAD, LCx], so any significant left main lesion alone makes arteries.size >= 2 and multivessel = true. A probe confirmed it: protected LM (patent LIMA to LAD) plus ad hoc gives anatomy {unprotectedLm:false, multivessel:true}, adhocAgainstReasons true and deferralApplies ['anatomy'], so a safety gap is raised. For an unprotected isolated LM the advocacy says 'with unprotected left main disease and multivessel disease'. The test 'a protected left main ... is not a deferral gap' asserts only anatomy.unprotectedLm === false, so it hides this.
findings.fix: Count multivessel disease from non-left-main lesions only: `for (const l of sig) if (l.vessel !== "LM") for (const a of lesionArteries(l, t.dominance)) arteries.add(a);`. Left main disease is reported separately through unprotectedLm. In report.test.ts, make the protected-LM case assert `adhocAgainstReasons === false` and `deferralApplies` toEqual [], and make the stable-LM ad hoc case assert that the advocacy does not match /multivessel/.

findings.problem: The form allows one worst-stenosis row per artery (LM, LAD, LCx, RCA), but truthReportOf passes every fixed lesion, segment by segment, to compareReport. Any second significant lesion on the same artery is therefore always listed under 'Missed' in the debrief's 'Your report' list and counted in meanBias, even when the learner reported the worst lesion correctly. Examples: LAD plus D1, tandem LAD 6 and 7, LCx plus OM, RCA plus PDA.
findings.fix: Build the study's truth report per finding row, keeping only the worst fixed lesion for each row. Rows: LM; LAD (LAD, D*, S*); LCx (LCx, OM*, RAMUS, and PDA/PLV when dominance is left); RCA. Pass that to compareReport. The alternative is to let the form add further lesion rows per artery. Add a test where LAD 80% (seg 7) and D1 70% (seg 9) are both present and the learner reports LAD 80% in seg 7: missed should be [] (or reflect only per-row truth).

findings.problem: The tree names septal perforators S1..S12, not SEPT*, so in a real session they fall through to `a === "LAD"` and are given ['anterior']. A probe on 40 CASE_LIBRARY cases showed 'S-branch walls: anterior' in every one; the septal tally is only LAD-main and PDA demand. PL2 and PL3 reach 'inferior' through RCA, contradicting the MODEL PARAMETER comment that posterolateral branches supply the lateral wall. SAN and AVN (atrial and nodal branches) are also counted towards LV walls. Truth is still right in the library cases, but only because LAD-main demand outweighs PDA.
findings.fix: In arteryOfVessel, add /^S\d+$/ and /^D\d+$/ to LAD. In wallsOfRegion, return ['septal'] for /^S\d+$/ (as for SEPT*), ['anterior'] for /^D\d+$/, ['lateral'] for /^PL(V|B|\d*)$/, and [] for SAN, AVN and /^RV\d*$/. Add a report.test.ts case using a real DiagnosticLabSession tree (session.engine.flow.regions) that asserts S1 regions map to septal.

findings.problem: When no lesion lies in the named segment, the function falls back to the most severe lesion anywhere on the artery. D1, D2 and OM targets also match LAD or LCx main-vessel lesions. Finding 10 (the `{ snapshots: [] } as unknown as ProcedureRecord` cast in withStudyReport). Both suggested fixes need files outside the package. Assessment (src/mentor/index.ts) carries no record and useAttending does not expose one. Having buildDebrief run the registered check would mean useAttending passing `report: studyReport.comparison` into assessAttempt (src/ui/lab/useAttending.ts). The only in-package alternative is fabricating a typed record with a fake RecordingMeta, which is no better than the cast. The cast stays local and documented: completeGap reads only snapshots, and the lab passes no onSeek, so the -6 to +4 s clip is never used. Reported as outOfScope.

problems.fix: Out of scope for this package; report it to the owner of caseGenerator/Simulator header. Give generated cases a neutral live name (e.g. 'Random case 7', with the pathology name shown only in the debrief), or have Simulator.tsx hide caseData.name until `finished`.

rejected: Finding 3 (header shows the generated case name, e.g. 'RCA — left main', during the finish step): rejected as out of scope for diag-study-report, as the finding itself states.
